channel.title: La Puce Libre — Microcontrôland (English)
channel.description: Microcontrôland's daily paper, written every evening by the gateway.

item.title: Day 35 — Wheat falls 3.2%
item.description: The Fields region watches its income melt away. The rest of the country feels it too.

item.title: Day 34 — Copper falls 3.0%
item.description: The Mines region watches its income melt away. The rest of the country feels it too.

item.title: Day 33 — Wheat slips 1.9%
item.description: The Fields region is keeping a close eye on its income. Its income is not returning the favour.

item.title: Day 32 — Copper edges up 1.6%
item.description: Nothing dramatic. The Mines region is doing its sums again, just in case.

item.title: Day 31 — President Niwata re-elected with 54%
item.description: Voters have chosen continuity. The palace stays in the Dam region. So does everything else.

item.title: Day 30 — Niwata leads the poll on 50%
item.description: Voting intentions: Niwata 50%, Naïkaïth 33%, Sakaïk 17%; nobody mentions Kouwou, Sita or Pisaï; of those asked, 8 intend to abstain. 20 citizens drawn by lot were asked at 20:00. At this sample size the margin of error is about 28 points. Readers are invited to bear this in mind, and will not.

item.title: Day 29 — Microcontrôland enters the age of Diplomacy
item.description: The civilisation reaches a milestone on day 30 of the era. The embassy opens: questions of the month and the ambassador's letter.

item.title: Day 28 — President Niwata re-elected with 75%
item.description: Voters have chosen continuity. The palace stays in the Dam region. So does everything else.

item.title: Day 27 — Copper soars 3.3%
item.description: The Mines region cashes in on the rise. The rest of the country feels it too.

item.title: Day 26 — Oil falls 2.6%
item.description: The Refineries region watches its income melt away. The rest of the country feels it too.

item.title: Day 25 — President Niwata re-elected with 63%
item.description: Voters chose continuity. The palace stays in the Dam region.

item.title: Day 24 — Niwata leads the poll on 63%
item.description: Voting intentions: Niwata 63%, Kiti 32%, Sita 5%; nobody mentions Naïkaïth, Kouwou or Sakaïk; of those asked, 1 intends to abstain. 20 citizens drawn by lot were asked at 16:00. With a sample this size, the margin of error is about 22 points. Interpret accordingly.

item.title: Day 23 — The country has a word for “freedom”: saïsa
item.description: At least five regions now say the same thing. The common language has 34 words.

item.title: Day 22 — Wheat falls 4.5%
item.description: The Fields region watches its income melt away, and the shock wave spreads across the country.

item.title: Day 21 — Opinion polls arrive. Opinions are expected to follow
item.description: Halfway through each campaign, twenty citizens drawn by lot will say how they intend to vote. The sample is small. The poll may be wrong. It may also be believed.
